gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 1 388369 Investigator tree, Queensland Museum.jpg
gallery.description:
Investigator tree, Queensland Museum
In November 1803, while Matthew Flinders' ship Investigator was anchored at Sweers Island, a crew member carved the name Investigator on the trunk of a tree. Other ships that visited the island during the next eighty years, including the Beagle in 1841, recorded their visits in the same manner on the trunk of the tree. in 1887 the tree was blown down during a cyclone, and soon after was procured for the Queensland Museum, Brisbane. (Description supplied with photograph.).
categories: Images from the State Library of Queensland

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 389221 Investigator Tree, Sweers Island, Gulf of Carpentaria, 1871.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 389221 Investigator Tree, Sweers Island, Gulf of Carpentaria, 1871.jpg
gallery.description:
Investigator Tree, Sweers Island, Gulf of Carpentaria, 1871
This photograph was taken in 1871 at Sweers Island, in The Gulf of Carpentaria, during the term of office of G.F. Sandrock as Sub-collector of Customs for the Gulf District (1866-1871). In the photograph, he is on horseback, second from the right. His wife is on foot infront of him, and his daughter, afterwards Mrs. B.A. Kent, is on horseback at the left of the picture. Portion of the tree is now in the Queensland Museum. G.F. Sandrock was transferred to Bowen in 1871, where his daughter married Mr. B.A. Kent, father of G.E. Kent, founder of the Bowen Tomato Industry, whose descendants still reside in Bowen (Description supplied with photograph.).
categories: Black and white photographs of Australia in the 1870s
Black and white photographs of Queensland
